english: The eight letters of the word EQUATION are rearranged, each letter being used exactly once. The number of rearrangements in which none of the five vowels E, U, A, I, O occupies the position that it occupies in the word EQUATION is
hindi: शब्द EQUATION के आठ अक्षरों को पुनर्व्यवस्थित किया जाता है, प्रत्येक अक्षर का ठीक एक बार प्रयोग करते हुए। उन पुनर्व्यवस्थाओं की संख्या, जिनमें पाँच स्वरों E, U, A, I, O में से कोई भी स्वर उस स्थान पर नहीं है जिस पर वह शब्द EQUATION में है, है
solution: Let $V_{x}$ = arrangements in which vowel $x$ keeps its place; $k$ given vowels fixed leave $(8-k)!$ arrangements
(Only the vowels are deranged; the consonants Q, T, N may stay or move, so the answer is not $D_{8}=14833$.)
solution_full: The vowels E, U, A, I, O occupy positions 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 of EQUATION. All $8!=40320$ rearrangements are considered.
For a vowel $x$, let $V_{x}$ be the set of rearrangements in which $x$ is in its original position. We need the number of rearrangements in none of $V_{E},V_{U},V_{A},V_{I},V_{O}$.
If a particular set of $k$ vowels is kept in place, the remaining $8-k$ letters can be arranged in $(8-k)!$ ways, so the intersection of any $k$ of the sets has $(8-k)!$ elements.
By the principle of inclusion-exclusion, the required number is $\sum_{k=0}^{5}(-1)^{k}\binom{5}{k}(8-k)!$.

This is a partial derangement: only the five vowel positions are forbidden, while the consonants Q, T, N may stay in their places. The full derangement number $D_{8}=14833$ would wrongly forbid the consonants too, and $D_{5}\cdot3!=264$ would wrongly keep the vowels among the vowel positions.
originality_note: New: a partial derangement of a word in which only the vowel positions are forbidden, so inclusion-exclusion runs over 5 of the 8 positions while all 8 letters move (way 5: derangement and inclusion-exclusion linked). Closest known: derangement of n letters into n envelopes, and 'vowels in alphabetical order / together' arrangements of EQUATION. Different because: the forbidden set is a proper subset of the positions, so neither D8 nor D5 is the answer.
blueprint_concepts: Principle of inclusion-exclusion for 2, 3 and n sets

concept_use.Principle of inclusion-exclusion for 2,: Inclusion-exclusion over the five events 'vowel x keeps its place', with intersections of size (8-k)!.
concept_use.Derangements: The count is a derangement of the vowel positions only (a partial derangement); D8 and D5 x 3! are the typical wrong answers used as distractors.
